name: Jonathan
overview: Jonathan was a male figure known as the son of Eliahba and identified as the twenty-fourth member of "the thirty," a distinguished group of David's warriors as recorded in 2 Samuel 23:32. Beyond these details, Scripture does not provide further information about his tribe or additional attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Jonathan means "gift of y-h-v-h," reflecting a theophoric element that honors the Lord. This proper name, as noted in 2 Samuel 23:32, highlights the recognition of God's gracious provision without indicating that the name was directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Jonathan is explicitly identified as the son of Eliahba according to 2 Samuel 23:32. Aside from this paternal relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Jonathan's role as one of David's thirty mighty men situates him among the elite warriors who supported David's rise to kingship. His inclusion in this group underscores his valor and loyalty during a critical period in Israel's history. Though not extensively detailed, his presence in this list contributes to the broader narrative of David's establishment as king under God's providence.
